questions.prompt: What is the difference between longitudinal and transverse movement?
questions.answer: Longitudinal movement runs along the spring line. Transverse movement runs across it.
rubric: Distinguish movement along the line from movement across it.

questions.prompt: Explain how a spring and a moving mass keep an undamped oscillation going.
questions.answer: The spring pushes or pulls toward equilibrium. Inertia carries the moving mass past equilibrium, so the spring is displaced the other way and pulls it back again.
rubric: Explain the restoring action toward equilibrium.
Explain how inertia carries the mass past it.

questions.prompt: Two models have the same mass and restoring stiffness but move in different directions. Must their frequencies differ?
questions.answer: No. They can repeat at the same rate when the moving mass and effective restoring stiffness match.
rubric: Explain that movement direction alone does not set frequency.

questions.prompt: Describe Mode 2 of the two-mass chain.
questions.answer: The masses move in opposite directions, alternately moving toward and away from one another. This strongly compresses and stretches the middle connection.

questions.prompt: What happens when two modes contribute movement in opposite directions at the same mass?
questions.answer: They partly cancel, or cancel completely if their displacements have equal size at that instant. Cancellation at one instant does not remove the original modes from the system.
rubric: Explain cancellation of the movements.

questions.prompt: For /i/, which effect dominates the first mode and which dominates the second?

questions.prompt: What happens to F1 and F2 for /a/ relative to the uniform reference?

questions.prompt: Why is strong air movement different from strong compression?
questions.answer: Neighboring air elements can travel together with little change in their spacing. Compression changes when their spacing closes and opens, which can happen strongly near a point with little movement of its own.
rubric: Distinguish movement of elements from changes in the gaps between them.
